_comment: Mock data for the web layer. Shape matches contracts/schema.md exactly. The 'audit' object is the audits/{auditId} document; 'findings' is the audits/{auditId}/findings subcollection flattened into an array. Four findings covering every UI state you need to build: f_001 a straightforward verified fix, f_002 a verified fix that still requires a human (render as 'needs a human', never as done), f_003 a visual finding axe cannot catch, f_004 a detected violation with no fix drafted yet (patchedCode is null — render as a finding with no diff). Draft 2 added 'status'; branch your UI on it rather than on 'verified'. Draft 4 renamed rgaaCriterion to regionalFramework + regionalCriterion — we measure WCAG globally and only NAME a regional framework as context (f_004 shows the null case). Draft 3 added announcedBefore/announcedAfter — what a screen reader says before and after the fix. Render those as the headline before/after: most fixes change no pixels, so this is where the change is actually visible. Null means the element carries no announced role (f_003, f_004), never that nothing changed.

findings.userImpact: Someone using a screen reader reaches the end of the contact form and hears only 'button', with no way to tell that it sends the message.
findings.changeSummary: Named the submit button and hid its decorative icon.
findings.announcedBefore: button: (nothing — announced only as its type)

findings.userImpact: A screen reader announces the filename 'team-photo-final-v2.jpg' instead of describing the team, so the person learns nothing from the image.
findings.changeSummary: Added an alt attribute requiring a human-written description.
findings.humanGuidance: Replace the placeholder with a description of what the photo actually shows and why it is on this page — for example 'The six-person A11ySentinel team standing outside the Antananarivo office'. If the image is purely decorative and adds nothing the surrounding text does not already say, use alt="" instead.
findings.announcedBefore: image: (nothing — announced only as its type)

findings.userImpact: The 'most popular' plan is marked only by a green border. Someone who cannot distinguish the colour sees three identical plans and no recommendation.
findings.evidence: The middle pricing card carries a 2px green border and no label, badge, or text distinguishing it from the two cards beside it.
findings.changeSummary: Added a text badge so the recommendation is not colour-only.

findings.userImpact: The footer text is too faint against its background to be read comfortably by someone with low vision, or on a phone in daylight.
